summary: Otoya Tanaka was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1924–1927). He taught Toshifumi Goto and held a post at Chuo University (~1957–1974).
Otto Blau was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott between approximately 1848 and 1852.
Otto Fischer worked in Sinology, Japanology, and history and archaeology. He held a post at the Kunstmuseum Basel in 1927 and at the University of Basel (~1927–1937), and taught Heinz Mode.

Otto Franke, a scholar of Sinology and Indology, studied at the University of Freiburg (~1882–1883) and the University of Göttingen (~1883–1887). He held posts at the University of Hamburg (~1910–1923) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1931).

Otto Höfler worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1921–1926) and Lund University (~1928–1934), later holding posts at Kiel (~1935–1938), Munich (~1938–1945), and Vienna (~1957–1971).

Otto Neugebauer studied at Graz (1919–1921) and Göttingen (1922–1926), working in history and archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Otto Rosenberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at St. Petersburg University (~1906–1911) under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Sergey Oldenburg, and later served as a professor there (~1917–1919).
Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at the philosophy faculty of the German University of Prague (~1913–1918) as a pupil of Moriz Winternitz.
Otto Strauss worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Paul Deussen (~1904–1908) and held a professorship at the University of Kiel (~1920–1928).

Indologist and linguist Otto von Böhtlingk studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1833–1835) and under Franz Bopp and Christian Lassen. He was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1842) and held a post at Jena (~1868–1885).

P. D. Premasiri, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied under Eliot Deutsch and at Ceylon, Canterbury, and Hawaii. He was a professor and head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Ceylon (attested 1999, 2010).

P. K. Mukhopadhyay works in philosophy and Indology. He was a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University and served as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Madras and under Nilakantha and Vaidyanatha, later serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Annamalai University (attested 1944).
Padmanabh S. Jaini was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor and professor emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1977–2016).
Palmira Brummett is a historian who studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago (~1981–1988). She held a post at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011).
Palmo Kyi is a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Rinzin Thargyal, Hanna Havnevik, and Per Kvaerne (attested 2012).

Pamela D. Winfield works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at Temple University (attested 2001) and as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Indologist Pandurang Vaman Kane studied at the University of Mumbai (~1898–1908). He held positions at Elphinstone College, Wilson College, and the University of Mumbai, and was the Government of India's National Professor of Indology (~1959–1972).
Parashuram Krishna Gode was an Indologist and historian who served as Curator at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1916–1946, ~1919–1961).
Parimal G. Patil works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard (~1989–1993) and the University of Chicago (~1993–2000), and held a post at Harvard University (~2005).
